subject: Kickstart: Hands-on POC scheduling, prompt review & load-test checklist
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Cho <anna@finapp.com>
Cc: Marcus Liu <marcus@finapp.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickstart: Hands-on POC scheduling, prompt review & load-test checklist

Hi Anna / Marcus,

Great to meet you on the demo yesterday — thanks for the thoughtful questions. Per our conversation, we'd like to run a short hands-on POC with your engineering team to validate routing, prompt performance, and an initial load test. Goal: get a working end-to-end integration and a perf snapshot you can share internally.

Proposed structure (high level):
- 2 x 2-hour working sessions (day 1: prompt routing & prompt tuning; day 2: load test & metrics)
- Pre-read: prompt examples + expected outputs, simple routing map, and load-test plan
- Deliverables: annotated prompt-suite, performance baseline, integration checklist

Would you be available for either of these pairs of dates?
- Option A: Tue/Wed 2027-04-26 & 2027-04-27 (US mornings)
- Option B: Tue/Wed 2027-05-03 & 2027-05-04 (US mornings)

I've attached a draft POC agenda and the current prompt-suite for your review. If procurement/IT needs a separate thread, happy to loop them in — just let me know.

Next steps: if one of the date pairs works, I'll coordinate internal leads and send a calendar pack + checklist.

Best,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Team — looping you in to lock the internal plan. Anna prefers Option A (Apr 26/27) but procurement needs a couple of days. I want to put a firm calendar hold now and finalize once procurement confirms.

Marissa: can you lead the hands-on prompt review and be our facilitator for day 1? Ben, please own day 2 load-test orchestration with the attached plan. Dev, we need your input on the runtime prerequisites and any KV/cache notes.

- Marissa: short facilitator slide deck + quick prompt classification table (intent / expected token ranges)
- Ben: load test config (target RPS, sequence length distribution, measurement hooks)

I'll draft the calendar invite with a checklist and a brief environment handshake window (15m) at the start of day 1.

Thanks — Sergio

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Cho <anna@finapp.com>
Date: 2027-04-14T14:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickstart: Hands-on POC scheduling, prompt review & load-test checklist

Quick technical notes — pulled from our runtime checklist:
- Network: we'll need the source IPs added to FinApp's allowlist (list attached in the drive link).
- Auth: please provision a service account with scope: inference.read, inference.execute; short-lived tokens preferred.
- KV/cache sizing: recommend initial KV capacity for session context at 2MB per concurrent session; this impacts batch sizing.
- Routing: for the hands-on we'll demonstrate a primary model and a lower-cost fallback (quantized) if latency > 350ms.

Ben — for load: target a ramp to 50 RPS sustained for 10 minutes, with 95th percentile token latency logged. We'll use the load_test-plan.xlsx counters.

I'll prepare a short ops checklist and paste it into the calendar invite.

— Dev

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
